newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow interested in Australia petrochem plant.
newsitem.headline: Dow interested in Australia petrochem plant.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co on Thursday expressed strong interest in establishing a world-scale integrated petrochemical plant in northwest Australia.
The group said it would make a formal submission to the Western Australia state government on building the plant in the Pilbara region, based on gas from the offshore North West Shelf.
"Dow is very interested in evaluating this opportunity as part of our focus on expansion into the Asia Pacific," Dow's managing director for Australia, Tino Giuffrida, said.
A Dow spokesman in Melbourne, Tony Jaques, told Reuters the plant would produce ethylene dichloride and caustic soda.
He could not immediately give any capacity dimensions for the proposed plant.
The Western Australia government last week called for expressions of interest in developing a A$1 billion petrochemical plant in the state's northwest.
It said it expected intense competition for the right to develop the so-called Pilbara Petrochemical Project from the world's major chemical-producing companies.
The state government said Royal Dutch/Shell, Germany's Krupp group and South Korea's Samsung had also expressed interest in such a development.
